sourceChecks.title: Experimental Study of Air Lubrication Method and Verification of Its Effect by Means of Sea Trial, MHI Technical Review Vol. 47 No. 3
sourceChecks.excerpt: maximum of 12 percent in a sea trial
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A full-scale module-carrier trial measured net energy savings of 8–12% for tested air-layer thicknesses after blower power was subtracted.
sourceChecks.limitations: One shallow-draft carrier and tested speeds/configurations only; does not show >80% skin-friction reduction, whole-wetted-surface continuous stability in all conditions, any-ship applicability, indefinite operation, or fleetwide fuel savings.

sourceChecks.title: Experimental investigation of vortex generator influences on propeller cavitation and hull pressure fluctuations
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Experiments measured propeller cavitation and hull-pressure fluctuations; a vortex generator changed cavitation onset and reduced some pressure-fluctuation effects.
sourceChecks.limitations: Cavitation remains in the tested configurations; no cavitation-free propulsor, 100% efficiency, all-speed/depth capability, or universal silence is shown.

sourceChecks.title: On the mechanism of marine fouling-prevention performance of oil-containing silicone elastomers
sourceChecks.locator: Results: Singapore Harbor; field tests; figures on fouling over 6–24 months
sourceChecks.excerpt: hard fouling organisms are completely absent
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Field panels of a silicone elastomer coating showed reduced hard fouling over observation periods up to 24 months, while soft fouling/biofilm remained.
sourceChecks.limitations: A limited coating/site test over months to two years does not establish complete organism exclusion, 30-year life, zero maintenance, zero environmental release, or projected fleet fuel/invasive-species impacts.

sourceChecks.title: Microbiologically influenced corrosion on naval carbon steel inside the hull of tugboats: a case study of prevention and control
sourceChecks.excerpt: Pitting corrosion was observed in all tugboats
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A case study found microbiologically influenced pitting corrosion on internal carbon-steel hull areas in three tugboats and discussed prevention/control measures.
sourceChecks.limitations: This documents corrosion and mitigation work, not zero corrosion across seawater, sediment and splash environments, all vessels, or full design life; economic/lifetime impact is not established.

sourceChecks.title: Experimental Result for a High-rate Underwater Acoustic Communication in Deep Sea for a Manned Submersible SHINKAI6500
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A sea trial with a manned submersible reported an underwater acoustic communication rate of 70 kbps at 3.6 km.
sourceChecks.limitations: The reported rate and range are below 1 Mbps at 10+ km and do not demonstrate links through ice or sediment, no repeaters, reliability, or real-time fleet control.

sourceChecks.title: The superconducting MHD-propelled ship YAMATO-1
sourceChecks.paraphrase: NASA’s record describes YAMATO-1 as a superconducting magnetohydrodynamic ship that completed sea trials in 1992.
sourceChecks.limitations: Bibliographic record supports prototype/sea-trial capability, but supplies no evidence of megawatt scale, >90% efficiency, practical deployment, or quantified silence.

sourceChecks.title: TopTier model tests and simulations on parametric roll behaviour of two large container vessels
sourceChecks.excerpt: model tests and simulations on parametric roll behaviour
sourceChecks.paraphrase: MARIN reports model tests and simulations examining parametric-roll behavior for two large container vessels and associated forecasting methods.
sourceChecks.limitations: Studying and forecasting roll does not establish elimination of parametric rolling or near-zero deck motion in any sea state, motion-sickness outcomes, or helicopter-operation safety.

sourceChecks.title: Hydrogen for Maritime Application—Quality of Hydrogen Generated Onboard Ship by Electrolysis of Purified Seawater
sourceChecks.locator: Abstract; Energy Observer onboard system description
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The paper evaluates hydrogen quality from onboard electrolysis of purified seawater aboard Energy Observer, with renewable electricity supply described for the demonstrator.
sourceChecks.limitations: This is a hydrogen demonstrator, not net-positive fuel production exceeding vessel propulsion demand; it does not establish ammonia/synthetic fuel, unlimited range, zero-emission operation, or independence from bunkering.

sourceChecks.title: Ship Hull Repair Using a Swarm of Autonomous Underwater Robots: A Self-Assembly Algorithm
sourceChecks.excerpt: verified within the two-dimensional Netlogo simulation environment
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The study proposes autonomous underwater robot modules assembling into a breach patch and tests the assembly algorithm in 2D simulation.
sourceChecks.limitations: The modules have no physical counterpart in the study; this does not show deployed shipboard autonomous self-healing/reconfiguration, battle-damage tolerance, continued vessel operation, or survivability.
